claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a Diablo-inspired aesthetic and art style reminiscent of classic isometric RPGs.

citations.review_text:
There is nothing fundamentally "wrong" with this game. I enjoy the Diablo aesthetic, the addition of NPCs, quests, and especially the design of bosses/ minibosses, with a variety of telegraphed attacks and AoE patters. It's also ridiculously cheap.

However...

30 minute runs in HoT seem to drag for eternity in comparison with the benchmark for this genre, which is Vampire Survivors. 
The equipment system is much too simplistic.
There seems to be an overreliance on the movement speed stat.
Sound effects are incredibly weak and the music is too monotonous.

It has great rogue-lite features, and nostalgia to the art-style that compares to classic Diablo 1 and Diablo 2. If you enjoy fast paced fun RPG-like isometric gameplay then you will enjoy this highly.

After a few runs, I still havent found any interesting upgrades that actually change how you build your character, save for one (increased damage with missing health). claims.claim: The game features a retro, pre-rendered aesthetic and sound design inspired by classic Diablo games.

citations.review_text: Survivors-like game built on Diablo 1-2 vibes

If you enjoyed Vampire Survivors or other bullet-heaven games, then this one is definitely worth checking out!

It has a great blend of Diablo II inspired art and sound design with the addictive gameplay loop that makes Vampire Survivors so much fun. It has plenty of its own ideas and personality, so it never feels like a copy.

There are loads of fun abilities to experiment with, challenging boss monsters to take on, and plenty of heroes to play. With 100+ achievements and plenty of replayability, and there’s a lot here to keep you coming back.

Highly recommended!

It's not remarkably different from VS but I like it a lot anyway. Nice crunchy Diablo graphics, janky in a 90s game kinda way, I think the enemies having nice animations and varied attack patterns helps it feel fresh, and I think the unlockable characters all feel different enough to make runs have some variety. 

I think if I had any feedback it would just be that the dialogue and book-reading text boxes are janky. But small complaint for a game that has proven to be a nice value

The Diablo 1-inspired pre-rendered aesthetic and atmosphere are genuinely excellent — one of the best visual identities in the survivor-like space. The early hours also deliver that classic “just one more run” pull. After enough time, though, the game reveals structural problems that make it hard to recommend over stronger alternatives in the genre.

The biggest issue is pacing and agency. Runs clock in around 25–30 minutes and a large portion of that time is spent in low-decision autopilot: clearing dense packs with the same abilities while waiting for the next meaningful spike. Unlike Vampire Survivors (which offers tighter loops and turbo options) or Death Must Die / HoloCure (which keep decision density higher and runs feeling more dynamic), Halls of Torment leans into deliberate slowness as part of its identity. What starts as atmospheric becomes repetitive and low-engagement once the novelty fades. By the later stages of a run you are often just waiting for the clock or the next boss rather than actively solving interesting problems.

Build variety is thinner than it first appears. A large share of the upgrade pool is straightforward stat increases. Transformative or synergistic choices exist, but they are outnumbered by incremental numbers that do not meaningfully change how a run feels. After a certain point most successful runs converge on similar solutions. Character differences matter, yet the overall decision space never reaches the depth that keeps the best games in this genre compelling across dozens of hours.

Meta progression compounds the problem. Unlocking characters, equipment, and meaningful power requires a heavy volume of runs. Some of the systems (artifact acquisition especially) feel opaque, turning the loop into pure grinding rather than directed progression. When the game has also shipped balance patches that nerfed the power curve while increasing enemy durability, the sense of earned strength that makes survivor-likes addictive is undercu…
Its vampire survivors with a fresh coat of paint inspired by diablo. BANGER

A really great variant on the Vampire Survivors mechanics, having lots of different interesting classes, a bunch of unique items and permanent unlocks with their gear systems and the cool Diablo 1 art style makes a really compelling experience. The game is extremely polished and worth picking up if you like those kinds of vampire survivors like games.

Went through all the levels (Unless something unlocks after finishing Agony mode for every level, which I'll get to eventually) and had a good time with it.  The aesthetics are fantastic, throwback to that 90's era, pre-rendered, PC gaming, feels very Blizzard-esque, but it's solid.  This is a Vampire Survivors clone, so if you played that game, you know what to expect from it, though it does a handful of things that I think help it stand out abit more on its own, but this isn't anything vastly different, which I'm cool with, I've dabbled in a couple of these types of games at this point, but aesthetically, this is probably the best looking one.

I saw that people had some bugs, maybe just with the DLC addition, but I didn't grab that and had zero issues with the game.  Definitely recommend it if you enjoy this type of game.

This game is really fun, the gameplay loop is pretty addictive and I love the art style of the game, big diablo vibes from it. I heard some not-so-good things about the dlc which sucks, so i dont plan on getting it, but other than that the game rocks.

This is Vampire Survivor's super cool older brother.

Whilst having some of the mechanics of VS, Halls of Torment goes a little further and does a few things differently, and those changes take what was a more casual & relaxed experience, and make it far more engaging.

Being able to aim your shots and the concept of sending items up the well to buy for future runs is a really cool idea, the equipment does interesting stuff, and the branching ability path upgrades make runs a bit more interesting.

The graphics hark back to the age of the old diablo games and retro CGI graphics, and I'm all for it, the art and sound design is nostalgic in all of the right ways.

If you enjoy VS, you'll no doubt enjoy Halls of Torment, 

Great job Devs! I hope that you can keep pumping out more content.

claims.claim: Runs feature a 30-minute timer where players fight through waves of enemies and bosses.

citations.review_text: fun and easy game to play and not think about much but it also has a few small things you can do in new and old maps that are like quests or story,  and they usually are found by following clues and stuff... the 30 minutes can sometimes feel too long for how strong the levels make you, so that anytime i would fight a cool or hard boss, i didnt have to dodge much because i just killed them too fast.

Cool game, 30-minute sessions, can be played with just a mouse. Lots of enemies.

So I need to update my review after getting a lot more information. It is a "Survivors-Like" genre but more in the traditional D&D style of characters: you unlock your Archer, Warlock, Cleric/Priest and there is a weird one "Exterminator" so far. 

How this differs from Vampire Survivors is this game actually tells you what the damage type is: physical, elemental, magic etc. Then it also will explain how your chosen upgrades will affect the abilities you also chose. So far this game seems a bit easier because the end bosses after 30 min are actually beatable without looking up guides or banging your head against it for hours on end. 

When you get a new piece of equipment you can send it up for use in a different run. Sure you lose it but that is the sacrifice you must make. You could also just keep it for current run but not have access on later runs.

It is a roguelite where you are upgrading your overall skills in between runs in a central hub area. 

The bullet hell aspect can still be a little difficult to differentiate between your effects and the enemy's since all of the sprites are so tiny. The game is super fun and addicting, perfect for Steam Deck.

claims.claim: Players can send unlocked equipment up via the Wellkeeper to use in future runs at a cost.

citations.review_text:
Recommended

As someone who enjoys survivor-like games, Halls of Torment has been a great experience. The similarities to Vampire Survivors are what got me interested in the first place, but the progression systems are what kept me playing.

What I like most is that every run feels rewarding, even when I fail. Completing runs earns coins that can be spent at the Strand of Blessings, which gives you permanent upgrades and makes future runs feel more manageable. There's always a sense that you're working toward something, and I never felt like my time was wasted.

The build variety is another big reason I enjoy the game. Between the different upgrades, abilities, and choices from the Wellkeeper, there are plenty of ways to approach a run. I found myself constantly experimenting with different combinations and trying to optimize my builds to see how powerful I could become. Finding a build that comes together perfectly is incredibly satisfying.

I also appreciate how the game handles progression beyond simple stat increases. As you continue playing, you unlock more options and systems that help with future runs. That steady sense of growth keeps the game engaging and gives you a reason to jump back in for "just one more run."

The dark aesthetic, the fast-paced gameplay, and the constant progression loop all work together extremely well. If you enjoy Vampire Survivors and other survivor-like games, Halls of Torment is easy to recommend. The build customization, permanent progression, and rewarding gameplay loop kept me hooked for far longer than I expected.

A fun, addictive game that always feels like it's making progress, even when you lose.

claims.claim: Multiple reviewers experience random crashes during gameplay, particularly on later characters and maps.

citations.review_text: the game crashed twice in a row

It's a fun game, but it's unplayable for me due to the fairly frequent crashes.

I have tried playing the game on 2 different computers and still crashes randomly on both.

It's a PS1/Diablo 2 era aesthetic of survivors-like; I like the variety in characters and overall gameplay loop a lot after having put ~100 hours into it when it was on Game Pass. My recommendation for the Steam version specifically is a "maybe" because this is the rare circumstance where the console version is better. Later characters/maps seem to cause this game to crash like mad. I've had multiple aborted runs now due to this, and will probably go back to the console version as a result. Worth picking up on a sale for a change of pace if you like survivors-style games but you may be better off grabbing it on console if you have the option as the stability is better.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a dark fantasy art style and aesthetic heavily reminiscent of the original Diablo games.

citations.review_text: A very interesting game that kept me hooked for a while. It really reminds me of the time I played Diablo 1 the atmosphere and graphics strongly evoke that game. I played the demo, and that specific Diablo vibe is what drew me in to buy it and I haven't regretted it.

Fun rogue....  lite/like? One of those. Very reminiscent of Diablo - graphically and musically. Very addicting and fun to chase that OP build where you can just stop moving and watch how everything just melts around you and then destroy a boss in 5 seconds - very fun... have I said that already? Because it is.

Never got bored just decided to move on with other games.

You don't play this game very often, but it gives you a very nostalgic Diablo vibe. It's perfect for people who don't have much time for Vampire Survivors but want cool, over-the-top battles. The game is also compatible with the Steam Deck and was made using my favorite engine, Godot.

My favorite title in the genre. Best Vampire Survivors-like/Bullet Heaven on steam imo and I've played at least a dozen of games like it. I like that you can aim, that adds more skill req to the game slightly while it still being mindless enough that you can watch a movie while you play. Build crafting is very fun and there's tons of skills and abilities for you to experiment with. There's 14 heros apparently. I've only unlocked like 10 of them at time of writing. I love how every single one feels completely different. I hope they continue putting out content including DLC and supporter packs because I intend to purchase everything the do. Last thing.... I love the old school Diablo aesthetic. LOVE IT. This game is so beautiful and fun to look at. I would say it's a solid 9/10 best of its kind right up there with the OG Vampire Survivors. If VS is kinda boring to you and you want something similar but a little more involved, this is the game for you. Would recommend it to anyone I think everyone can enjoy this. I would like a little more challenge and hope there's a harder end game. I have breezed through it to this point. I think out of my 15 or so runs I've died maybe like 2-3 times. Most of the time I steamroll even on the harder to start characters like Warlock or Shield Maiden. So I'm really hoping after I unlock all characters maybe the game gives me a more difficult mode where enemies are more numerous and have more health. Maybe even give us a mode where we jump start to level 10 but enemies are 10x beefier. 


edit: at original time of writing I'm more like 8-10 hours into the game. I fell asleep with the game launched still and didn't turn it off until I got back home from work like 22 hours later.

Halls of Torment feels like the closest thing we have to a Dungeon Crawler Carl game right now. Essentially a Diablo-skinned Vampire Survivors, it’s a nonstop Skinner box of violence and numbers, constant achievement unlocks and level-ups, paired with satisfying metas and character building for gameplay that (stripped bare) is essentially a bullet hell with autoattack. And despite that, I like it more than some other Diablo-esque action RPGs, which are essentially the same thing but with active abilities and %-based lootmaxing. 

You pick a hero archetype and descend into an endless themed dungeon. Your goal is to survive 30 minutes and defeat the final boss. Enemies come at you nonstop and become an uncountable horde as the timer ticks down. At countdown milestones, bosses and minibosses spawn in and pursue you until dead. There’s a miniquest the first time you go to each floor and other than OBJECTIVE: SURVIVE your only other direction is markers that point toward power-ups. 

Your only ability to interact with the world is through moving and attacking. Everything else comes from leveling up your character by collecting loot from dead enemies. This is doubly interesting because it means that killing enemies isn’t enough; you need to go stand where they were (which is typically under the horde coming at you) AND ALSO the level-ups have a surprising amount of depth because certain upgrades only appear on certain level-ups. Even at high levels the level-ups come often enough to always be satisfying, especially the powerup that collects all the money currently on the ground throughout the entire dungeon. 

Between missions, there are meta unlocks like starting with equipment, potions, permanent upgrades for all heroes, permanent upgrades for specific heroes, and level-specific unlocks. It all works, and it reinforces that Halls of Torment is just a well-made, well-optimized horde killer game. It’s fun for a few hours and worth the price of admission, though by y…

A really good game. There's a lot to do considering there are 500 achievements to get so 100% completion may take a while. If u like Vampire Survivors or Diablo 2 u should check this game out. It's highly domapine-inducing so i doubt u will get bored easily but i think there should be more maps for the base game. So far i had so much fun with this game. 8.5/10
This game is best in class. If you like Survivorlikes and enjoy the retro Diablo 1 aesthetic it's an easy recommend this is the best Survivorlike I've played, and I've played a fair few.

A Dark-Fantasy Gem

I can’t say enough good things about Halls of Torment. After more than 40 hours, I’m still having an absolute blast with it.

This game simply oozes charm. It feels like a genuine love letter to classic PC gaming, game development, and dark fantasy.

Art Style and Atmosphere

The art style is fantastic, the atmosphere is wonderfully dark, and the music fits perfectly. Its environments and character models take me back to an older era of gaming, with a dark-fantasy feeling reminiscent of Warcraft II, but without the technical limitations or performance problems of that time.

Even when the late-game Torments become incredibly chaotic and the screen fills with enemies and effects, the game continues to run beautifully. In more than 40 hours, it hasn’t failed me once.

Classes and Gameplay

Every class feels distinct, the builds are fun to experiment with, and there’s enough variety to keep each run feeling fresh.

It’s the perfect “log in, do a run, and go about your day” kind of game—although, admittedly, I’ve been addicted to the gameplay loop ever since I bought it.

Storytelling and Discovery

I love the game’s light but atmospheric storytelling. It never overwhelms you with exposition, but there’s still enough voiced dialogue, environmental storytelling, and visual progression to make the world feel alive.

Certain changes happen naturally as you play, eventually leading you toward completely new areas and bosses. The game trusts you to notice these things for yourself, which makes discovering them feel much more rewarding.

After about 20 hours, I thought I had seen nearly everything the game had to offer. Then it continued surprising me.

The Bard

The biggest surprise came when I finally unlocked the Bard.

Until that point, the classes had mostly followed recognizable fantasy archetypes. There’s absolutely nothing wrong with that—the game executes those archetypes extremely well—but it also created a certain expectation. When I selected th…

Survivor Type that looks like Diablo 1/2
Neat characters, a lot of items, quite a lot of ways to set up various builds.

Huge meta-game progression: 
You have to do runs to retrieve equipment from the maps.
Killing bosses gives you shards with which to further boost your characters.
Torment mode also slowly unfolds by collecting Artifacts that modify and make the runs more difficult.

If you want to see everything, you will grind *a lot*.
But even if you don't care about grinding and just want to fire up a casual round the game holds up well.

In my opinion, beats Vampire Survivors out of the park.

This is a very fun and well done vampire survivors-like.  There are lots of different character classes that enhance the combat and make each class feel distinct. It has a very Diablo'ish look and feel, but has its own unique combat and progression.  Great weapons and abilities to help you conquer the levels too. The end-game is solid and you can delve into it as deeply as you want.  My only wish is that there is more of a cohesive campaign, it's just kind of "there" and doesn't provide much guidance about what you're supposed to be doing.  I'm 40 hours into it and I still don't know what I'm working towards or how I should be tackling the maps/areas. 

There have been a few free updates that add to the game and provide more hours of gameplay.  I am betting if you like VS, you will definitely enjoy this one too.

As a lover of Vampire Survivors, I figured I'd like this and meant to pick it up at some point. Well, I finally did, and I adore it! It has the same addictive style, just with a Diablo coat of paint.. which as a lover of Diablo, that's pretty cool.
Fun to play, remind me the good old Diablo 1 long plays.

9.5/10 This game was a fricken blast non stop grinding it for achievements and items it was so much fun. 100% steam achievements. Maybe will check out the dlc in the future but definitely an amazing game! Great soundtracks.
Art style is good also its very similiar to the old diablo games. Amazing aesthetic. The npc's are also really well voiced!

Great vampire survivors like game if you pay a bit attention to the quests and track them the progress system is rewarding. Give it a chance if you like games like megabonk deep rock galactic survivor etc it also has this diablo1 2 like vibe.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that individual runs have a long duration, with some expressing a desire for shorter map lengths or ways to speed up the timer.

citations.review_text:
I really enjoy Halls of Torment. It’s simple, fun, and easy to get into. There are plenty of different characters, and each one feels enjoyable to play in their own way.

My only issue is that some runs feel a little too long, sometimes lasting 30 minutes or more. I think 15 to 20 minutes would be a better length.

Overall, I’ve spent more than 30 hours with the game and had a great time. It’s actually a very relaxing game for me. Simple, enjoyable, and definitely worth playing.
Highly addictive. Just like Vampire Survivors in Diablo look - the individual runs feel a tad long, othern than that fantastic game.
could use alot more maps and a way to shorten the level like a potion or something to shave a couple minutes off the timer. Lots of variety in the different abilities(traits) you can get.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features hundreds of achievement unlocks and a structured quest tracking system tied to progression.

citations.review_text: A good bullet heaven game. The upgrades unique to each class nudge you towards different playstyles, and the equipment system lets you shape the start of your run, or pivot by swapping them out with new equipment mid-run. There are a LOT of unlockables and achievements, so if you're here to play to completion, you'll be grinding these out for quite a bit of time.

Great vampire survivors like game if you pay a bit attention to the quests and track them the progress system is rewarding. Give it a chance if you like games like megabonk deep rock galactic survivor etc it also has this diablo1 2 like vibe.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as having a very slow initial pace that can make early progression feel tedious or unfriendly to beginners.

citations.review_text:
There is something about this game, which makes me love it, even though it's flaws continue to bug me. Sure, it's extremely unfriendly to beginners, and it takes a lot to get your feet moving, but once you figure it out, progress is so much more rewarding than easier/ simpler titles. 

*The slime enemies look like moving turds. No redeeming qualities there.

Vampire survivors but at 10% speed.

Edit: Alright it's not that bad. It is slower than most if not all other survivors (at least the 10+ I've played) and sadly the fastest to get boring. I found myself sick of the long boring afk runs at around 7 hours in, where i initially gave it a negative review. I kept giving it chances and it turned out to have some interesting challenges. Another thing is that at first you're bombarded with 20-30 achievements per run so the achievements lose their value really, but when you delve deeper it's quite the opposite and you need to have an entire run dedicated to a specific achievement to get it, and you're not even guaranteed to get it because often it requires some RNG, which gets very tedious. Kind of an awkward design that beats the survivor-like purpose which is to be a dopamine dispenser, so it's got itself in a weird state.

Overall the game has a lot of stuff to offer, a lot of interesting mechanics, and a nostalgic Diablo 1-like style. Yes, everything is very slow but the game still has its charm, and it excels at what it wants to be, which is a more laid-back survivor-like. Worth it, especially for the price.

If there were a Steam award for "Game I Never Thought I'd Love", it's HoT. 

I have no memory of buying it or what compelled me to buy it. I never played the original Diablo games, and I hated playing Diablo III. This game, though, I absolutely cherish and adore. To say it's grown on me is putting it feather gently.  

It starts off so slow, just a couple skeletons trudging along to punch you in the face.

Before you know it, 30 minutes later your screen is absolutely ablaze with the chaotic fire of millions of pixels; frantically running and dodging fire demons and evil cubes shooting purple magic goo. You're escaping by millimeters and praying for that one more small 0.2 m/s speed increase, because you just need to hold out for thirty more seconds and your health is hanging on by a thread.

It's completely B A N A N A S and I love it. Not to mention the music loops are straight bangers, and I will die on this hill. Ember Grounds goes hard.

Cannot recommend this game highly enough.

citations.review_text: Fantastic game, the stylization along with the gear system makes doing crazy runs on this feel rewarding. the accessibility is also fantastic you can choose to have everything auto i.e. aiming and shooting but it also allows you to feel like you're playing the game if you're feelin a bit zesty and don't want to shut your brain off. solid 8/10

Halls of Torment feels like the closest thing we have to a Dungeon Crawler Carl game right now. Essentially a Diablo-skinned Vampire Survivors, it’s a nonstop Skinner box of violence and numbers, constant achievement unlocks and level-ups, paired with satisfying metas and character building for gameplay that (stripped bare) is essentially a bullet hell with autoattack. And despite that, I like it more than some other Diablo-esque action RPGs, which are essentially the same thing but with active abilities and %-based lootmaxing. 

You pick a hero archetype and descend into an endless themed dungeon. Your goal is to survive 30 minutes and defeat the final boss. Enemies come at you nonstop and become an uncountable horde as the timer ticks down. At countdown milestones, bosses and minibosses spawn in and pursue you until dead. There’s a miniquest the first time you go to each floor and other than OBJECTIVE: SURVIVE your only other direction is markers that point toward power-ups. 

Your only ability to interact with the world is through moving and attacking. Everything else comes from leveling up your character by collecting loot from dead enemies. This is doubly interesting because it means that killing enemies isn’t enough; you need to go stand where they were (which is typically under the horde coming at you) AND ALSO the level-ups have a surprising amount of depth because certain upgrades only appear on certain level-ups. Even at high levels the level-ups come often enough to always be satisfying, especially the powerup that collects all the money currently on the ground throughout the entire dungeon. 

Between missions, there are meta unlocks like starting with equipment, potions, permanent upgrades for all heroes, permanent upgrades for specific heroes, and level-specific unlocks. It all works, and it reinforces that Halls of Torment is just a well-made, well-optimized horde killer game. It’s fun for a few hours and worth the price of admission, though by y…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game experiences crashes during runs, resulting in the complete loss of progress due to the absence of a save system.

citations.review_text: I played this game time to time in years. I can say this , this game just crashes in some of the couple runs(Not unplayable level). If things get too many I guess ?? .Ofc I don't know the reason I know that when I spent 300k gold or something for vault run(half of my money) then I got crashed very quickly.(I had safe run before that run) I added so many multistrike , slow and fragile debuff also every elemental in one of the run it crashed again very close to the end run(was doing sage's missions)(Also had clear runs before). Well if it did save I wouldn't complain this much - this could be an okay game comment .But hell no. You just loose your run which is very annoying. At the very beginning of this game I think I didn't had such problems. But there were only 3-4 maps or something. Something seems broken to me .Well I'm not gonna try to complete the game like this for sure. No matter what skills or heroes you guys gonna bring it wouldn't solve my problem so. I read somewhere 1440 p monitor causes more crashes (I don't know how accurate it is but mine is like that) drivers are also up to date and heat is like a fridge. also I don't have crashes on other games. like 4-5 other games I played this month. Well last thing, I thank you for the game you guys did. I had good time so far but yeah. That's the end for me .

I really wish I could give HoT a good review because it offers everything I want out of a roguelike. Unfortunately, the game crashes out of nowhere, and since there's no saving during runs that means a crash always kills the player's progress dead. That's doubly infuriating considering runs take typically take more than half an hour to complete, as you're just out all that time if a crash comes near the end. Turning down my settings helped for a bit but the game just crashed AGAIN when I was four minutes away from beating a stage I'd been trying for days to get past. Recommendation to avoid until a much more stable version is released.
